scalability problem. Instead of doing that
column2: move most of the code to be

column1: protected by the i_lock instead. The exceptions are the global lists

->fl_link is what connects these structures to the
global lists
column2: so we must ensure that we hold those locks when iterating

column1: over or updating these lists.
Furthermore
column2: sound deadlock detection requires that we hold the

column1: blocked_list state steady while checking for loops. We also must ensure
that the search and update to the list are atomic.
For the checking and insertion side of the blocked_list
acquisition of the global lock into __posix_lock_file and ensure that
checking and update of the  blocked_list is done without dropping the
lock in between.
On the removal side
column2: when waking up blocked lock waiters

column1: global lock before walking the blocked list and dequeue the waiters from
the global list prior to removal from the fl_block list.
With this
column2: deadlock detection should be race free while we minimize

column1: excessive file_lock_lock thrashing.
Finally
column2: in order to avoid a lock inversion problem when handling

column1: /proc/locks output we must ensure that manipulations of the fl_block
